_comment: Pinned third-party binaries for the Windows build. Hashes are SHA256 of the exact vendored builds. Build-Runtime.ps1 verifies bin/*.exe against these hashes and refuses to package a mismatch. Setup.ps1 and the CI 'Fetch vendored binaries' step download each tool from a VERSIONED url (never 'latest'), so a pin stays valid until it is deliberately upgraded - pins to 'latest' used to break CI every time upstream shipped a release. To upgrade a tool: change the version in the url here AND in Setup.ps1 and .github/workflows/build.yml, update the hash, and test the app end-to-end, all in one commit.

yt-dlp.exe._note: Back on the stable channel (was temporarily on nightly for https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17456, fixed upstream). Hash matches yt-dlp's published SHA2-256SUMS. Same version as requirements-app.lock.txt.

deno.exe._note: REQUIRED, not optional - yt-dlp shells out to this as its JS runtime to pass YouTube's anti-bot/signature challenge. Without it, downloads fail with HTTP 403. Not referenced by name anywhere in our own scripts, which is exactly why it got dropped once already - don't repeat that mistake.
